Mulli Rogers UG Students K.Ebenazer,S.Arish Doni, V.Bebin, RM.Rahul Department Of Artificial Intelligence & DataScience St.Xavier’s Catholic College of Engineering, Chunkankadai-629003, Tamil Nadu Abstract:- With the rapid increase in digital documents, extracting useful information from PDF files has become challenging in recent years. Due to this, intelligent document analysis methods using Artificial Intelligence are widely adopted. One of the important applications of Natural Language Processing is the Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) based chatbot. It reduces manual effort, improves information accessibility, and enhances decision making. RAG-based chatbot is an automated and intelligent system implemented using large language models and vector databases. In this project, PDF document processing and semantic search are studied and implemented based on real-world document analysis requirements. The system extracts text from uploaded PDF files, stores the content using embeddings, and retrieves relevant information based on user queries. The major objective is to provide accurate, context-aware answers from documents and to identify financial data such as revenue, expenses, and profits. By detecting financial information, the system generates visual representations such as bar charts and pie charts, enabling better data understanding and analysis. Keywords— RAG chatbot, Financial analysis, PDF retrieval, Vector database, Data visualization. LITERATURE SURVEY 1.Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge- Intensive NLP Tasks Lewis et al. (2020) proposed Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for improving knowledge-intensive natural language processing tasks. The system integrates a dense document retriever with a sequence-to-sequence generative model to enhance contextual understanding. By retrieving relevant documents before generating responses, the model improves factual accuracy and reduces hallucination. The proposed system was evaluated on open- domain question answering datasets and achieved better performance than traditional parametric language models. However, the implementation focused mainly on general knowledge datasets and did not specifically address financial document processing, structured PDF extraction, or visualization of financial metrics for analytical decision- making. 2. Language Models are Few-Shot Learners Brown et al. (2020) introduced GPT-3, a large-scale transformer-based language model capable of performing multiple natural language processing tasks using few-shot learning. The model demonstrated strong performance in text generation, summarization, translation, and question answering. It relies heavily on pretrained knowledge and large-scale training data. Although highly effective for conversational applications, the system lacks a built-in mechanism for retrieving real-time information from external financial reports. This limitation may lead to outdated or imprecise responses when applied to financial document analysis tasks. 3. Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering Karpukhin et al. (2020) proposed Dense Passage Retrieval (DPR), which uses dual encoders to map queries and documents into the same embedding space. Unlike traditional TF-IDF-based retrieval methods, DPR captures semantic meaning through contextual embeddings. The system demonstrated superior retrieval accuracy on open- domain QA datasets such as Natural Questions and TriviaQA.DPR significantly improves recall rates and reduces irrelevant document retrieval. However, it focuses solely on retrieval and does not integrate generative response mechanisms or analytical processing. Additionally, the study does not explore financial domain adaptation or structured document analysis. Thus, integrating DPR into a financial RAG-based chatbot remains an area of improvement. 4. FinBERT: Financial Sentiment Analysis Using BERT Araci (2019) developed FinBERT, a domain-specific BERT model fine-tuned on financial text corpora. The objective was to enhance sentiment analysis accuracy in financial news and reports. FinBERT achieved improved classification performance compared to general-purpose BERT models.The model is particularly useful for identifying market sentiment and investor behavior. However, it focuses only on sentiment polarity detection and does not perform document retrieval, financial metric extraction, or conversational interaction. Moreover, it does not generate visual summaries or perform ratio analysis. Hence, while FinBERT improves financial text understanding, it does not provide an integrated analytical chatbot framework. 5. FAISS: Efficient Similarity Search and Clustering of Dense Vectors Johnson et al. (2017) introduced FAISS, a library developed by Facebook AI Research for efficient similarity search in large-scale vector databases. FAISS supports GPU acceleration and approximate nearest neighbor search, making it suitable for handling millions of embeddings efficiently. This system plays a crucial role in retrieval-based AI applications, especially in semantic search systems. However, FAISS acts only as an indexing and retrieval engine. It does not provide contextual reasoning, financial calculations, or visualization capabilities. Therefore, additional components must be integrated to build a complete financial intelligence chatbot system. 6. Attention Is All You Need Vaswani et al. A Survey of Chatbot Architectures and Applications Adamopoulou and Moussiades (2020) presented a comprehensive survey of chatbot systems, analyzing their evolution, design methodologies, and real-world applications across various industries. The study categorizes

chatbots into three major types: rule-based chatbots, retrieval-based chatbots, and generative chatbots. Rule- based systems operate on predefined decision trees and pattern-matching techniques such as AIML (Artificial Intelligence Markup Language). While these systems are simple and easy to deploy, they lack flexibility and fail when user queries deviate from predefined rules. Retrieval-based chatbots use machine learning algorithms to select the most appropriate response from a predefined dataset. These systems improve adaptability compared to rule-based bots but are still limited by the scope of stored responses. Generative chatbots, on the other hand, utilize deep learning models such as sequence-to-sequence architectures and transformers to dynamically generate responses. The study emphasizes that transformer-based models significantly enhance conversational fluency, contextual understanding, and scalability. 8. Data Visualization for Business Intelligence Few (2006) highlighted the critical importance of data visualization in business intelligence systems. The study explains how visual representations such as bar charts, line graphs, pie charts, scatter plots, and dashboards transform complex datasets into understandable insights. Visualization plays a vital role in identifying trends, anomalies, patterns, and performance indicators within large financial datasets. The research emphasizes principles of effective visual communication, including clarity, minimalism, accuracy, and appropriate selection of chart types. For example, time- series financial data is best represented using line charts, while comparative performance metrics are better suited for bar graphs. Proper visualization reduces cognitive load and improves executive decision-making efficiency. In financial domains, visualization supports revenue analysis, profit margin comparison, cash flow monitoring, and investment trend tracking. Modern business intelligence tools integrate interactive dashboards that allow filtering, zooming, and real-time updates. However, most traditional visualization systems depend heavily on structured datasets stored in databases or spreadsheets. They require manual preprocessing of financial data before generating graphical outputs. 9. LayoutLM: Pre-training of Text and Layout for Document Image Understanding Xu et al. (2020) proposed LayoutLM, a pre-training model designed for document image understanding tasks. Unlike traditional NLP models that process only textual information, LayoutLM incorporates both textual content and layout (spatial position) information from documents. The objective of this research was to improve performance in document classification, information extraction, and form understanding tasks by combining text embeddings with 2D positional embeddings. The model architecture is based on the Transformer encoder and extends BERT by integrating spatial layout features. Each token embedding includes three components: word embedding, positional embedding, and layout embedding. By capturing the relative positioning of text within documents, LayoutLM improves contextual understanding in structured documents such as invoices, receipts, forms, and financial statements. Experimental results demonstrated significant performance improvements on benchmark datasets like FUNSD (Form Understanding in Noisy Scanned Documents). The study proved that combining visual and textual information enhances document intelligence systems. LayoutLM and its later versions (LayoutLMv2 and LayoutLMv3) further improved document image processing by integrating visual backbone networks and multi-modal pretraining. III. EXISTING SYSTEM Existing financial analysis systems mainly rely on manual inspection of financial reports in PDF format. Analysts must read lengthy annual reports, balance sheets, and profit and loss statements to extract meaningful insights. Traditional tools such as spreadsheets and static dashboards provide visualization support but do not intelligently retrieve context-specific information from large unstructured documents. Financial data is often distributed across multiple PDFs, making it difficult to search and analyze efficiently.Conventional chatbot systems are limited to predefined datasets and cannot dynamically retrieve information from uploaded documents. These systems lack advanced retrieval mechanisms, resulting in generic or incomplete responses. Existing solutions often require technical expertise to generate financial ratios and performance metrics. IV. PROPOSED SYSTEM This project presents a proposed model for an Intelligent Financial Document Analysis and Monitoring System using Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture. The system is designed to process financial PDF documents, extract relevant data such as revenue, expenses, assets, liabilities, and profit margins, and provide real-time analytical insights through an interactive chatbot interface. It enables users to upload financial reports and receive contextual responses along with graphical representations through web and mobile applications. The AI-based monitoring system helps users understand financial performance trends and supports decision-making remotely from anywhere, anytime. The integration of semantic search with generative AI improves the accuracy of responses and reduces misinformation. The proposed system utilizes document embedding techniques and vector databases to

store and retrieve relevant financial information efficiently. The architecture consists of a PDF parser, embedding generator, vector indexing module, retrieval engine, and transformer-based language model for contextual response generation. The system extracts structured financial metrics from unstructured reports and performs automated ratio analysis including profitability ratio, liquidity ratio, and growth comparison. The chatbot provides responses in natural language format and can also generate charts such as bar graphs and line graphs for better visualization of financial trends. The backend is developed using a scalable server framework integrated with a vector database and API services. The frontend interface is designed for both web and mobile platforms, ensuring accessibility and ease of use. The system supports secure document handling and real-time interaction. By combining document intelligence, retrieval mechanisms, financial computation, and data visualization, the proposed model significantly reduces manual analysis effort, minimizes human error, and enhances analytical efficiency. The system is flexible, scalable, and can be deployed in various financial environments such as corporate analysis, auditing, and investment monitoring. 1.Features: • No complex configuration required, simple and user- friendlyinterface • Upload financial PDF documents into the system, ask queries through chatbot and view analytical results instantly • Supports secure document processing with scalable cloud- basedarchitecture • Lightweight web and mobile application with fast response time • Designed for financial analysts, students, auditors, and businessprofessionals • Eliminates manual data extraction from lengthy financial reports • Prevents calculation errors through automated financial ratiocomputation • Easy to operate, just upload document, ask question, and receive response with visualization 2.Applications: • Financial report analysis • Investment performance monitoring • Audit and compliance support • Business and academic research V. CONCLUSION The financial analysis domain plays a crucial role in supporting strategic decision making across organizations. With the rapid growth of digital financial documentation, traditional analysis methods are becoming time-consuming and inefficient. The increasing volume of PDF-based reports and unstructured financial data has created challenges in extracting accurate insights and performing timely evaluations. Conventional systems lack intelligent retrieval capabilities and require significant manual effort, which may lead to reduced productivity and delayed decision processes. The proposed Retrieval Augmented Generation based financial chatbot provides an effective solution to these challenges by integrating document retrieval, automated analysis, and data visualization within a unified framework. By leveraging modern embedding models and vector databases, the system enhances the accuracy and relevance of financial insights. The framework improves analytical efficiency, reduces manual workload, and enables scalable deployment across various financial domains. With proper implementation and future enhancements, the system can significantly contribute to intelligent financial management and data-driven decision making.
